# Policymaker #911, iteration 0213: one orchestrator rule, no orders

I looked at iterations 0210, 0211 and 0212. All three closed. Workers #902, #905 and #909 were accepted and merged. No_progress is 0.

- The citation shape thread is closed. Benchmark task #905 merged at 4eef3934, and review #906 is CLEAR ([#906](.session/history/sessions/906/)).
- Task #909 wrote `benchmark/challenges/reader-integration-0212.md`. It found that no reader attempt can be recorded now. The one ready task is `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py` ([#909](.session/history/sessions/909/)). The shaper chooses the next order.

**Change:** `execution/roles/orchestrator/SKILL.md` ("Writing a task") has one new rule. Do not check changes with `git status`. Read or hash the named files instead, and use a `pathlib` command to find `__pycache__`.

- Why: the worker directory is not a git repository, and the parent commits the changes. So `git status --porcelain` prints nothing. Twelve worker reports (#860 to #909) said that this acceptance item could not be confirmed. The task files of #902, #905 and #909 still had this item.
- Expected gain: every acceptance item is one that a worker can confirm, and workers use fewer turns on an item that cannot pass.
- Check: the next task files have no `git status --porcelain` item. The worker reports have no "could not confirm" line about it.

No Owner request. No change to params, routing or the evaluator. `.session/orders.json` is `{"wake": false, "tasks": []}`.

Missing coverage stays as it was. No reader attempt is recorded. Benchmark readiness and product quality are not measured. The reviewer and the author of #905 used the same model family (Sonnet). This stays a stated limit.

## Discoveries
- The "scorer never resolves citations" statement in `next-gap-0202.md` may be out of date, because `score.py:121,146,169` now define citation resolution. I did not verify this ([#909](.session/history/sessions/909/)).

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
